newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ICI delivers 90 mln stg savings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ICI delivers 90 mln stg savings.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI) said on Thursday its giant cost-cutting programme was on track and that 90 million stg in savings were delivered during the first nine months of this year.

Finance director Alan Spall told Reuters in an interview that staff numbers worldwide during the third quarter fell by 950 or by almost four percent over the nine months, with the cuts falling mainly in its paints and titanium dioxide arms.
The UK accounted for around 15 percent of these numbers.
ICI took a 137 million stg exceptional charge at the half year point to accelerate its cost-cutting programme, which aims to slash expenses by 400 million stg by the end of next year.
"We're continuing to invest because we're pump priming the savings that will come through in 1997. The overall programme though we're confident about and we're on track," said Spall.
He said the goup had delivered 90 million stg in savings at a pre-tax level over the first nine months of the current year.
ICI earlier reported that pre-tax pre-exceptional profits nearly halved in the third quarter to 131 million stg from 248 million stg.

It said in the results statement profits from the industrial chemicals sector came under intense pressure due to sharply lower selling prices, particularly in polyester, titanium dioxide and chlorine. Rising oil prices also affected margins.
Of the polyester market, Spall said however that the fourth quarter was showing signs of modest gains in volume.

"All of the evidence now is the destocking is starting to fill up again and, while there is still surplus capacity, the fourth quarter is actually probably going to look a little better from the volume point of view," he said.
Spall added that prices in the container plastics market of polyester could erode further during the fourth quarter, but PTA or pure terephthalic acid was unlikely to see further declines.

A record result during the third quarter from ICI's paints division, where trading profits jumped to 57 million stg from 32 million was due to better than expected earnings from recent acquisitions, he said. Sales rose 24 percent in the nine months.
